chunks: From him, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥasan, from his father ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام about a man who recites in the bathhouse and has intercourse in it. He said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam Mūsā عليه السلام, the authority from whom the ruling is transmitted
key_terms.الْحَمَّامِ: the bathhouse; the setting in which the ruling is being asked about
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; a formula indicating permissibility
key_terms.يَقْرَأُ: he recites; referring here to recitation in the bathhouse
key_terms.يَنْكِحُ: he has intercourse; referring to marital intercourse in that place

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite and have intercourse in a bathhouse according to Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Imam Mūsā عليه السلام concerning two acts in the bathhouse: recitation and intercourse. The Imam عليه السلام states that there is no harm in either, indicating permissibility in this context.
